mkdir -p /work/.github/workflows && cat > /work/.github/workflows/build-and-consume.yml <<'EOF'
name: Build and consume artifact

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Produce build output
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          echo "Built from ${GITHUB_SHA} at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > dist/build-info.txt
          echo "hello from the build job" > dist/app.txt

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  consume:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Wait for build to finish; without this the jobs run in parallel
    # and the artifact won't exist yet.
    needs: build
    steps:
      - name: Download artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist/

      - name: Use artifact
        run: |
          ls -la dist/
          cat dist/build-info.txt
          cat dist/app.txt
EOF

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/build-and-consume.yml` with two jobs. The file parses as valid YAML, but I haven't linted it with `actionlint` (it isn't installed here) or run it on GitHub.

- **`build`** writes some files to `dist/` and uploads them with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` under the name `build-output`. The step is set to fail if there are no files to upload, and GitHub keeps the artifact for 7 days.
- **`consume`** has `needs: build`, so it waits for `build` to finish. It then downloads the artifact with `actions/download-artifact@v4` into `dist/` and reads the files.

How it works:
- **`needs:` is required.** Without it the two jobs run at the same time, and the download fails because the artifact doesn't exist yet.
- **Upload and download must use the same `name`.** If you leave out `name` on download, it downloads every artifact from the run, each into its own subfolder.
- **Upload and download must use the same major version (v4 here).** Artifacts uploaded with v4 can't be downloaded with v3, and the reverse.
- **The download only finds artifacts from the same workflow run.** To get one from a different run or workflow, add `run-id` and `github-token` to the download step.

To use it in a real project, replace the "Produce build output" step with your actual build command and set `path` to your output folder. Nothing is committed yet; tell me if you want me to commit it.
